title: Slicing a cone: circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola
examples: How do you get a parabola from a cone?
What is the difference between an ellipse and a hyperbola?

stages.label: A double cone
stages.note: Two cones tip to tip, like party hats.

stages.label: Flat cut: circle
stages.note: Cut straight across the cone.

stages.label: Tilt: ellipse
stages.note: Tilt the cut a little: a stretched circle.

stages.label: Steeper: parabola
stages.note: Cut parallel to the side: an open U.
stages.ask: How do you get a parabola from a cone?

stages.label: Steepest: hyperbola
stages.note: Cut through both cones: two curves.
stages.ask: What is the difference between an ellipse and a hyperbola?

explain.say: Take a cone, like a party hat, and imagine another one balanced on its tip, upside down. Now slice through with a flat knife. Depending on the angle, you get four different curves! Look at the first stage: the double cone.

faq.a: The curves you get by slicing a cone with a flat plane: the circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola.

faq.q: How do you get a parabola from a cone?
faq.a: Slice the cone with a plane parallel to its sloping side. The curve opens out and never closes.

faq.q: What is the difference between an ellipse and a hyperbola?
faq.a: An ellipse is a closed oval from a gentle tilt. A hyperbola comes from a steep cut through both cones and has two separate open branches.

faq.q: What are the equations of the conics?
faq.a: Circle: x squared plus y squared equals r squared. Ellipse: x squared over a squared plus y squared over b squared equals 1. Parabola: y equals a x squared. Hyperbola: x squared over a squared minus y squared over b squared equals 1.
asks: What is the equation of an ellipse?

faq.q: Where do conic sections appear in real life?
faq.a: Planet orbits are ellipses, thrown balls follow parabolas, satellite dishes are parabolic, and some cooling towers and lamp shadows are hyperbolas.

facts: The four conic sections are the circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola.
Apollonius of Perga wrote a famous eight-book work on conic sections around 200 BCE and gave the ellipse, parabola and hyperbola their names.

quiz.say: Which conic do you get by cutting a cone straight across, parallel to its base?
quiz.show: Which conic do you get by cutting a cone straight across, parallel to its base?
quiz.why: A flat cut across the cone gives a circle.

wrong.1: A parabola needs a cut parallel to the sloping side.
wrong.2: A hyperbola needs a steep cut through both cones.

quiz.say: Which conic has two separate branches?
quiz.show: Which conic has two separate branches?
quiz.why: The hyperbola cuts both cones, so it has two pieces.

wrong.0: An ellipse is one closed oval.
wrong.2: A parabola is one open U.
